title: Register a tenant as a configurable process (pilot skeleton: steps of the target process)
description: SKELETON, NOT RUNNABLE YET (dry_run blocked_by pilot-not-built; the owner's pilot, spike D-175). It lists in business order what the registration of a tenant must do once it runs as the definition platform.register_tenant of the platform tenant: validate input, create tenant, provision schema and migrate, bind realm and administrators, notify by e-mail, end (s1 to s6); then the configurability proof: edit the definition through the designer API to add an e-mail and a file notification, start again, see the mail, roll back in one step (s7 to s14); a forced failure with a retry (s15 to s18); the refusals of a company user (s19 to s22) and the no-bypass check (s23). TODAY the process is route code (executed_by direct) and the routes answer 201, not 202; every `says` line is the target, and the 'today' column is in the map row BP-PLATFORM-01. The request bodies and answer fields of the new starts are drafts: they are fixed when the pilot builds the proof, from the code and its route tests. Cleanup (delete and purge the created tenants, back to the previous definition version, no open instance) is written then, with the platform residue check.

steps.says: TARGET: the platform administrator opens the platform tenant's definitions and sees the process 'platform.register_tenant' with its versions; v1 is active (item 1). TODAY no such definition exists.

TARGET: from the 'Register tenant' screen's call the platform administrator registers a tenant; the answer is 202 with the id of a process instance of platform.register_tenant (item 2). TODAY this call creates the tenant directly and answers 201.

The steps of the instance, in order: validate input, create tenant, provision schema and migrate, bind realm and administrators, notify by e-mail, end. The timeline shows each with who, when, result, duration (items 2 and 4).
The new tenant exists and is active; the second start path, the tenants API, also starts an instance (item 9).
Item 9: the tenants API (the second of the five paths) answers 202 and starts an instance of the same definition.
The instance of the second start ended; its timeline carries the same steps.
Configurability (a): with no notification step the first instance ended and no mail is sent (item 6). The platform administrator remembers the active version.
Configurability (b): through the designer API the administrator creates a draft of the definition that adds a notification step with the e-mail channel to a catcher address and the file channel.
The draft is checked before it is activated; a notification step whose address is not allowed, or a file step that names a path, is refused (items 6 and 8).
The administrator activates the draft; the first instance stays on version 1.
Configurability (c): a new registration is started again.
The mail arrives in the mail trap (the runner reads the trap by recipient and subject; the body is masked in the log).
The file written by the file channel is read from the tenant's own notification files area (it is under a server-generated name).
Rollback in one call to the previous version; a fourth start sends no mail (item 6 d).
Failures (item 7): a registration with a realm the probe refuses leaves the instance in ERROR.
The timeline names the failed step and the kind of failure; no token, realm credential or mail body appears in it.
A dead-letter entry exists for the failed step.
The administrator retries it after the cause is fixed; the instance ends; a second retry changes nothing.
Security (item 8): a company user is refused when starting the registration; the answer is the uniform refusal.
A company user cannot create a version of the definition.
A company user cannot roll the definition back.
A company user cannot read the instances of the process; the answer for an instance of another tenant is the same as for an unknown one.

No bypass (item 9): the tenants of steps s2, s5 and s11 each have an instance of the process; none was created by a direct path. The proof is the source-scan callers test and the route test named in the map row.
